title: Accelerating AI on Edge — Chintan Parikh and Weiyi Wang, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: A Google DeepMind product talk on running Gemma 4 E2B/E4B models on-device via the LiteRT framework, covering edge use cases (voice agents, local skills, image/audio), cross-platform deployment, and NPU acceleration. It is a platform/marketing overview for mobile and IoT developers, not a talk about agent orchestration, review quality, or cloud cost control.

takeaways.what_they_do: They describe architectures where a small on-device model handles local inference and a separate orchestration layer decides which work runs locally versus in the cloud, with the edge model able to call external APIs for the rest.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's orchestration to decide what should run locally or not and not uh and should run elsewhere

takeaways.technique: Small quantized models for narrow tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue small (2B/4B) quantized models are sufficient for narrow, low-latency tasks like summarization and structured extraction, reserving bigger models for heavier work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: 4B is going to be a little more heavy duty if you're looking to run on bigger platforms like laptops or IoT devices
takeaways.numbers: E2B ~1-2GB RAM; NPU 3-10x perf; up to 13x accelerator boost; 35x faster than Llama on mobile
